characters.summary: Gothmog is the Lord of Balrogs and High Captain of Angband, wielding a fiery whip and a black axe in melee combat. He is an ancient demon of immense physical might and command over fire and shadow.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to exceptional physical strikes from mighty heroes like Ecthelion
limitations: Destroyed permanently when drowned in deep water while locked in combat with Ecthelion

sources.supports: General attributes, weapons, and death at the hands of Ecthelion.

feats.claim: Slew Fëanor, High King of the Noldor, in single combat before the gates of Mithrim.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Chapter 13: Of the Return of the Noldor

feats.claim: Slew Fingon, High King of the Noldor, during the Nirnaeth Arnoediad.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Chapter 20: Of the Fifth Battle

notableResults.note: Ambushed with the aid of other Balrogs.
Fought alongside other Balrogs to overwhelm Fingon.
Mutually assured destruction; Ecthelion drove his spiked helm into Gothmog, dragging both into a fountain.

campaignTags.claim: Gothmog is a creature of fire and wields a fiery whip.

unknowns: Exact dimensions of his physical form beyond being a giant demon of terror.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings, J.R.R. Tolkien
characters.summary: Gríma Wormtongue is a counselor and spy who fights through poison, treachery, psychological manipulation, and stealthy knife attacks rather than open combat.
weaknesses: Physically weak and cowardly when confronted directly by capable warriors.
limitations: Zero proficiency in open military combat or facing armed opponents.

sources.supports: Role as counselor, dagger usage, and cowardly nature.

feats.claim: Subverted King Théoden of Rohan through prolonged poisoning and counsel.
Murdered Saruman at Bag End with a knife after years of abuse.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Scouring of the Shire

notableResults.note: Stabbed Saruman from behind while Saruman was walking away humiliated.

campaignTags.claim: Acted as a secret spy and saboteur within the court of Rohan.
Operates through stealth, poison, and betrayal.

unknowns: Exact chemical composition of the poisons used on Théoden.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings, J.R.R. Tolkien
characters.summary: Gwaihir the Windlord is the greatest of the Great Eagles of the Third Age, using massive talons, crushing beak strikes, and supreme aerial mobility to dominate the skies.

mechanisms: Thick feathers and armor of speed and altitude

weaknesses: Vulnerable to ranged weapons like great arrows or siege engines if grounded or caught at low altitude.
limitations: Cannot operate effectively in cramped underground environments.

sources.supports: Status as Windlord, rescue feats, and combat capabilities.

feats.claim: Rescued Gandalf from the pinnacle of Orthanc.
Rescued Frodo and Sam from the slopes of Mount Doom.

notableResults.note: Fought off Nazgûl in the skies above Mordor alongside Landroval.

campaignTags.claim: Gwaihir is a giant eagle with natural wings and flight.
Carried Gandalf and other riders on his back.

unknowns: Exact wingspan and physical lifting capacity limits.

characters.summary: Huan is a divine hound from Valinor endowed with speech, preternatural speed, strength, and immunity to ordinary weapons, capable of overcoming master beasts and werewolves.

mechanisms: Fated protection against all weapons save the greatest wolf ever born

weaknesses: Fated to die after speaking three times in his life.
limitations: Fated to die after uttering three prophetic words.

sources.supports: Origins in Valinor, prophecy of death, and feats against Sauron and Carcharoth.

feats.claim: Defeated Sauron in his wolf form at Tol-in-Gaurhoth.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Chapter 19: Of Beren and Lúthien

feats.claim: Tracked and hunted any quarry without fail.

notableResults.note: Pinned Sauron by the throat until Sauron surrendered the fortress.
Mortally wounded Carcharoth in a vicious duel, but died of his own wounds.

unknowns: The exact nature of the Valian magic that empowered him.

characters.summary: Húrin Thalion, Lord of Dor-lómin, is one of the greatest mortal warriors of the Elder Days, fighting with a heavy battle-axe and possessing endurance granted by Morgoth's curse to witness his family's ruin.
weaknesses: Human mortality and vulnerability to overwhelming numbers without supernatural endurance active.
limitations: Subject to human physical limits once overwhelmed by scores of opponents.

sources.supports: Prowess with battle-axe, Nirnaeth Arnoediad last stand, and endurance.

feats.claim: Slew seventy trolls of Gothmog's guard during the retreat at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Chapter 20: Of the Fifth Battle

feats.claim: Stood alone in a rear-guard action, killing every orc that approached him while shouting 'Aurë entuluva!'

notableResults.note: Killed seventy trolls before being buried alive under a pile of slain enemies.

unknowns: The precise mechanics of Morgoth's curse-induced survival.

characters.summary: Idril Celebrindal is an Elven princess of Gondolin who relies on wisdom, foresight, and stealth rather than direct martial combat.
weaknesses: Lacks heavy armor or specialized martial combat training for front-line battle.
limitations: Not a dedicated combatant or warrior queen.

sources.supports: Lineage as Turgon's daughter, role in the Fall of Gondolin.

feats.claim: Successfully foresaw the doom of Gondolin and prepared the Secret Way for refugees.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Chapter 23: Of the Tuor and the Fall of Gondolin

feats.claim: Fought off Maeglin during his attempt to kidnap her and Eärendil.

notableResults.note: Resisted and thwarted Maeglin with aid.

campaignTags.claim: Organized the secret escape route (Ithil) for survivors of Gondolin.

unknowns: Extent of her direct combat feats.

characters.summary: Irmo, known as Lórien, is one of the Valar, the master of visions, dreams, and desires, wielding potent divine magic over the mind and spirit.
weaknesses: Bound by Eru's decrees regarding direct intervention in Middle-earth.
limitations: Does not engage in physical warfare or direct combat.

sources.supports: Status as Vala, master of dreams and visions.

feats.claim: Created the Gardens of Lórien in Valinor, filled with soothing illusions and resting places for gods and elves.

campaignTags.claim: Irmo is a Vala wielding supreme divine magic and mastery over dreams.
Has complete dominion over sleep, visions, and mental rest.

unknowns: Direct combat capabilities outside of mental and dream manipulation.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings, J.R.R. Tolkien
characters.summary: Isildur is a Dúnedain warrior and King of Gondor and Arnor, fighting with a sword and armor, famously cutting the One Ring from Sauron's hand.

mechanisms: Invisibility granted by the One Ring

weaknesses: The One Ring corrupts his judgment and betrays his position when worn.
limitations: Vulnerable to ambush when relying solely on the Ring for escape.

sources.supports: Role in cutting the Ring from Sauron, death at Gladden Fields.

feats.claim: Cut the One Ring from Sauron's hand using the broken hilt of Narsil.
Planted a seedling of Nimloth the White Tree in Minas Anor.

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion / Fellowship of the Ring
notableResults.note: Cut the Ring from Sauron's hand after Sauron was already defeated by Elendil and Gil-galad.

campaignTags.claim: Wielded and wore the One Ring.
Became invisible when wearing the One Ring.

unknowns: Exact details of how he survived the ambush at Gladden Fields before losing the Ring.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings, J.R.R. Tolkien
characters.summary: Khamûl the Easterling is the second-in-command of the Nazgûl, wielding a Morgul blade, fear aura, and dark sorcery to terrify and incapacitate opponents.

mechanisms: Wraith form immunity to normal mortal weapons

weaknesses: Vulnerable to fire and magical light, particularly Elven magic.
limitations: Power wanes in broad daylight without magical reinforcement.

sources.supports: Status as second of the Nazgûl, Easterling origin, and abilities.

feats.claim: Ruled Dol Guldur in Sauron's absence and hunted the Shire for the One Ring.
feats.citation: Unfinished Tales / The Lord of the Rings

feats.claim: Drove out the kings of Rhûn and served as Sauron's lieutenant in the East.
feats.citation: The Lord of the Rings Appendix

campaignTags.claim: Wields wraith-sorcery and the Black Breath.
Rode winged beasts and fell steeds.

unknowns: His exact name and history from the Second Age prior to taking a Ring of Power.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings, J.R.R. Tolkien
characters.summary: Landroval is a giant Great Eagle of the Misty Mountains, fighting with massive talons, beak, and superior flight speed alongside Gwaihir.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to concerted ranged attacks or siege weapons.
limitations: Cannot fight effectively in tight underground spaces.

sources.supports: Identity as brother of Gwaihir and participation in the battle at the Black Gate.

feats.claim: Participated in the assault at the Morannon and helped rescue Frodo and Sam from Mordor.

notableResults.note: Assisted Gwaihir in intercepting the Nazgûl above Mount Doom.

campaignTags.claim: Landroval is a Great Eagle with natural wings and flight.

unknowns: Specific individual feats independent of Gwaihir and Thorondor's lineage.
